segments.say: Let's breathe together for a little while. There's nothing to get right. Simply notice the air coming in through your nose, cool and soft. And notice it going out again, a little warmer, a little slower. In, and out. You don't need to change anything. Just let the breath find its own easy rhythm, the way the tide finds its way up the sand.

If you'd like, you can count gently. Breathe in for a count of four. One, two, three, four. And breathe out for a count of six. One, two, three, four, five, six. The longer out-breath tells your body that it's safe to settle. That the day is done. Let's do it once more. In for four. And out for six. Slow and easy.

As you breathe, thoughts may drift through your mind. That's perfectly natural. Imagine each thought as a small cloud, floating slowly across a wide evening sky. You don't need to catch it, or push it away. Just watch it drift, and let it pass. Another may come. Let it drift too. The sky stays wide and calm, whatever floats across it.

Here's a simple rhythm to come back to, any time you lose your place. Breathe in slowly. Breathe out slower still. That's all there is to it. No technique to master. No goal to reach. Just a slow breath in, and an even slower breath out, again and again, until your breathing hardly needs you anymore.

show.text: Breathe in slowly. Breathe out slower still.

segments.say: Now, as your breathing slows, let a landscape come gently into view. Imagine you're standing at the edge of a wide, open meadow, just as the sun is setting. The air is mild. The grass is soft and long, moving a little in a light breeze. In the distance, there are low hills, rounded and gentle, turning gold and then rose in the evening light.

Picture it clearly, or let it be soft and blurred. A meadow at dusk, a narrow path winding through the grass towards the hills. The sky above is turning from gold to soft lilac. There's nobody else here. Nowhere you need to be. Just you, the path, and the quiet evening light, slowly fading.

Let yourself begin to walk along the path, very slowly. There's no destination. You're not going anywhere in particular. Each step is unhurried, light and easy. The grass brushes softly against your legs. The ground is warm from the day's sun. With each step, you feel a little more at ease, as if the path itself is carrying you gently forward.

And as you walk, notice how your mind begins to loosen, just like it did for the walkers in that study. Thoughts come and go easily. Nothing feels urgent. The rhythm of your steps, one and then another, becomes a kind of quiet music. Your mind is free to wander wherever it likes, across the meadow, over the hills, up into the soft evening sky.

Notice the small things along the way, slowly, one at a time. Soft grass. Warm ground beneath your feet. A gentle breeze on your face. Hills turning gold, then rose, then a deep, quiet blue. And high above, if you look, a first star, just beginning to shine. Each one a small, calm thing. Each one enough.

Somewhere nearby, you hear a little stream. Its water runs quietly over smooth stones, never hurrying, never stopping. You walk towards the sound, and find the stream running alongside the path. The water is clear and calm. It moves at its own pace, the way your breath is moving now. In, and out. Over the stones, and on.

Perhaps you'd like to sit down for a while beside the stream. The grass is soft and dry. You lean back a little, and feel the earth holding you, steady and patient. There's nothing more to walk towards. You've arrived, simply by stopping. The stream keeps flowing. The sky keeps darkening, softly. And you rest.

Let that thought settle into you for a moment. You've arrived, simply by stopping. There's no next thing you need to reach. No problem to solve before you can rest. The rest is already here, right now, in the meadow, by the stream, under the first stars. All you have to do is let yourself have it.

The last of the evening light is fading from the hills now. Their shapes become soft and dark against the sky. The meadow grows quiet. A few more stars appear, one by one, as if someone were slowly lighting tiny lanterns across the sky. The air is cool and kind. Everything around you is settling into night.

Notice your breath again, if you like. It's probably slower now than when we started. Deeper. Softer. Each breath in is easy. Each breath out lets go of a little more of the day. You don't need to count anymore. Your body knows exactly what to do. It has been breathing for you all your life, through every busy day and every quiet night.

Let the day slip away now, piece by piece. Whatever happened today, whatever was said, whatever is left undone, it can all wait until morning. It will still be there tomorrow, if it matters. And you'll meet it rested. Tonight, it can simply float away, like a leaf on the little stream, carried gently downstream, out of sight.

Watch them float away, one by one, on the little stream. Today's worries. Unanswered messages. Unfinished jobs. Tomorrow's plans. Each one drifting gently downstream, getting smaller and smaller, until you can hardly see it at all. They're not gone forever. They'll be waiting in the morning. But for now, the stream has carried them away.

Your body may be feeling heavier now, and warmer. Your arms resting. Your legs resting. Your head sinking a little deeper into the pillow. That's good. That's exactly how it should feel. In a little while, we'll travel slowly through the body, softening each part. But for now, just enjoy this heaviness, this warmth, this quiet.

Stay by the stream as long as you like. Listen to the water over the stones. Watch the stars appear. Breathe in slowly, and breathe out slower still. If you drift off here, in the meadow, under the sky, that's perfectly alright. The stream will keep flowing, and the night will keep you safe, until morning comes, gently, in its own time.
